The digest has two triggers. In [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/instrumentation.ts), `register()` starts the in-process scheduler on the Node.js runtime. `startScheduler()` and `tick()` in [src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts) check every minute and enqueue a `digest-email` job on a 60-minute cadence; `drain()` and `runHandler()` in [src/server/jobs/queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatch it to `runDigestEmailJob()`. Separately, a platform scheduler can POST to [src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts); its `POST()` checks the `x-taskflow-cron` secret and calls the same job directly.

In [src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts), `runDigestEmailJob(now)` first asks `listOrgIdsForRollup(50)` for candidates. That function in [src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts) selects at most 50 organizations with usage rows, oldest measurement first; it is not a scan of every organization. For each candidate, the job loads the organization, and `shouldRunForOrg()` requires it to be unarchived and its configured `digestHourUtc` to equal the current UTC hour. It then checks `digest_email` with `isEnabled()` and `buildFlagContext()`. The flag in [src/config/feature-flags.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/config/feature-flags.ts) requires at least the Growth plan, unless the organization has the enabled override.

For each due organization, `listDigestRecipients()` in [src/server/services/digest-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/services/digest-service.ts) calls `listDigestSubscribers()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts). It selects distinct user IDs with **at least one** preference row in that organization whose `digestOnly` is true. It does not require that row’s `email` setting to be true or check membership status. The preference action in [src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts) checks the feature flag when someone enables `digestOnly`.

The material for a digest has already been recorded as notifications. `registerFanOut()` in [src/server/services/notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/services/notification-service.ts) subscribes to events such as assignments, overdue issues, comments, mentions, and member joins. Its handlers call `notify()`, which deduplicates recipients, excludes the event’s actor, looks up each person’s preference for that kind, resolves allowed channels, and inserts a notification row when at least one channel remains. A person who muted all channels for an event therefore gets no row for it.

For each subscriber, the job sets a rolling window from `now` minus 24 hours through `now`, then calls `buildDigest()`. It reloads the organization and rechecks the flag. `listUnreadSince()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts) fetches that recipient’s unread rows created at or after the window start, newest first. `buildDigest()` excludes rows after the window end, maps their ID, kind, title, link, and creation time into `DigestEntry` values, and keeps the first 50. Selection uses **all** qualifying unread rows; it does not filter them by the kinds marked `digestOnly` or by their stored channels.

If at least one entry remains, the job loads the user, calls `renderDigest()`, and passes the result to `sendEmail()`. There is an implementation distinction in the output: `renderDigest()` passes the organization ID, recipient name, entry count, window bounds, and first title to `renderEmail()` in [src/server/services/email-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/db18ee3f-c0bf-49c3-a351-e11b784d19fb/src/server/services/email-service.ts). That function renders a generic table of those properties; this path does not call the separate `DigestEmail` component or render the full entry list. `sendEmail()` currently logs an `email.sent` record and has no outbound mail transport. After it returns, the job marks each included notification read, then increments its processed count.

A subscribed person is skipped when the organization is not selected in the usage batch, is missing or archived, is outside its configured UTC hour, or no longer has the digest flag enabled. They are also skipped if their user record is missing or `buildDigest()` finds no qualifying unread entries: for example, there was no notification, it was already read, it fell outside the rolling window, or fan-out excluded or muted it. A successful previous run marks its included rows read, so a repeat run with no other qualifying rows has nothing to send. Errors for an individual recipient are logged and counted as failures; processing continues with the next recipient.
